chapter.chapterTitle: Sex Expression, Pollen Drift & Seed-Set Investigation
chapter.learnerQuestion: What reproductive structures are present, when and where could pollen have been released, and what evidence supports an internal or external explanation for seed set?

sourceContext.citation: Nimmala M, Ross SD, Foroutan H. Cannabis pollen dispersal across the United States. Scientific Reports. 2024;14:20605. doi:10.1038/s41598-024-70633-x.
sourceContext.supports: Windborne cannabis pollen deposition has a steep near-source decline but a long dispersal tail, with strong seasonal, regional and day/night variation. Uniform isolation distance cannot guarantee zero cross-pollination.

sourceContext.citation: Hermaphroditism in Cannabis sativa L.: Impacts, Inducers, and Industry Implications. 2026.
sourceContext.supports: Cannabis sex expression is plastic and affected by genotype, developmental state and environmental context; intersex expression can create unintended pollen and seed set, and early detection is important.

sourceContext.citation: THC Genetics & Breeding companion literature and Outdoor V6 reproductive-risk lessons.
sourceContext.supports: Source-reported lineage, observed sex expression, intended pollination and uncertain parentage must remain separate evidence categories in breeding and crop records.

subtopics.lessonTitle: Inspect reproductive structures systematically instead of checking one branch once
subtopics.goal: Quantify sex-expression observations across plants, nodes and flowering stages so male or intersex structures can be detected and tracked before seed set is used as the first warning.

measure.unit: count and % of defined crop population
measure.method: Use a repeatable route and record which plants were actually inspected. Include lower, interior and late-developing branch positions rather than only top flowers.
measure.frequency: At defined reproductive-stage checkpoints and more frequently when unexpected structures are found.

measure.unit: count by female / male / intersex-suspect / unknown class
measure.method: Count observed structures using macro photos for uncertain cases. Keep sex-expression class separate from plant identity and do not label an uncertain structure as confirmed pollen-producing tissue without adequate evidence.

measure.unit: % plants with confirmed or suspect intersex structures
measure.method: Record confirmed and suspect counts separately, each divided by plants inspected.
Record the first date and developmental stage for each plant where unexpected reproductive expression is observed.
measure.frequency: At first observation and updated if expression changes.

record: recent stress or intervention context without assuming causation
compare: genotypes or cohorts under the same environment
confirmed intersex incidence vs suspect incidence
interpret: Sex expression should be recorded as an observed phenotype, not automatically attributed to one stress event or one genetic cause.
A single missed inspection can matter because reproductive structures can develop in hidden or late-forming sites.
Repeated expression within a genotype or family is stronger breeding evidence than one isolated observation, but environment and developmental timing still belong in the record.
subtopics.decisionRule: Increase inspection intensity when unexpected reproductive structures are observed and keep the plant identity traceable. Make removal, breeding or containment decisions according to the project's reproductive goal and legal/site protocol rather than from an unverified photo alone.
subtopics.confidenceCheck: Young floral structures and damaged tissue can be misidentified. Use repeat observations or expert/macro confirmation before high-confidence classification.

subtopics.lessonTitle: Audit internal pollen sources before blaming neighboring fields
subtopics.goal: Map pollen-producing structures, likely release timing and crop movement so an internal source is investigated before external pollen is treated as the default explanation.

measure.method: Record confirmed male or pollen-producing intersex plants/branches separately from suspect structures.
measure.frequency: At discovery and every follow-up reproductive survey.

measure.unit: count or ordinal abundance class by plant/branch
measure.method: Record whether pollen structures are closed, opening, empty/released or unknown. Photograph representative stages before handling when practical.
measure.frequency: Every inspection of a known source.

measure.method: Map the location of confirmed internal pollen sources relative to later seed-set clusters or susceptible flowers.
measure.frequency: Once a source or seed-set cluster is identified; update if additional sources are found.

measure.method: Compare likely pollen-release dates with the period when nearby female flowers were receptive. Keep uncertain dates labeled estimated.
measure.frequency: During source investigation and after new evidence.

record: structure stage: closed / opening / released / unknown
first and last observed source dates
wind condition during observed release when known
crop work or handling event near source
compare: seed-set distribution near vs far from confirmed internal sources
timing of source release vs female susceptibility
windward/downwind pattern during known release windows
interpret: A confirmed pollen-producing plant inside the crop is a plausible source but still may not explain every seeded flower.
Spatial proximity and timing overlap strengthen an internal-source hypothesis; absence of either weakens it.
Removing a source after pollen release does not erase the earlier exposure window, so source history must be retained.
subtopics.decisionRule: Complete an internal-source audit before assigning seed set to external drift. Preserve release timing, location and affected-zone maps so later parentage or crop-quality investigation has usable evidence.
subtopics.confidenceCheck: Field mapping can establish plausibility, not genetic parentage. DNA-based parentage testing would be needed for high-confidence attribution to a specific pollen donor.

subtopics.lessonTitle: Treat external pollen as a weather-and-timing risk, not a fixed radius
subtopics.goal: Quantify neighboring pollen sources, wind-source overlap and flowering timing so external cross-pollination risk is described dynamically rather than by one isolation-distance number.

measure.metric: Known or suspected external source distance and bearing
measure.method: Map known hemp/cannabis pollen sources or likely source sectors relative to the crop. Label unverified sources as suspected.
measure.frequency: Before flowering and whenever neighboring land use becomes known or changes.

measure.unit: % observations or hours with source sector upwind
measure.method: Using on-site or clearly labeled nearby weather data, count defined observation periods when wind travels from the source sector toward the crop during the reproductive overlap window.

measure.unit: days of overlapping pollen release and female susceptibility
measure.method: Record best-known flowering/release timing for the external source and crop. Mark modeled, reported and directly observed dates separately.

measure.unit: pollen count per validated sampler area/time or lab result
measure.method: Where an appropriate pollen sampler and identification method are available, preserve sampler location, exposure duration and identification method. Do not treat generic dust capture as confirmed Cannabis pollen.
measure.frequency: During targeted high-risk windows when the method is available.

record: source identity or suspected source sector
rain or weather events affecting the period
compare: periods with vs without source-sector winds
different external sources by timing and direction
external-risk pattern against the internal pollen-source audit
interpret: The 2024 dispersal model shows a steep decline in deposition near source but a long tail with meaningful seasonal, spatial and day/night variation.
Distance alone cannot establish zero risk; source size, weather, release timing and receptive flowering overlap all matter.
A mapped source and favorable wind create exposure plausibility, not proof that a particular seed was fathered by that source.
subtopics.decisionRule: Rate external pollen risk from source confidence + distance/bearing + timing overlap + wind overlap. Avoid declaring any universal distance completely safe and keep unresolved origin explicitly unresolved.
subtopics.confidenceCheck: Weather models and neighboring-crop reports add context but do not directly measure pollen deposition at the flower. Direct sampling or genetic parentage testing provides stronger attribution.

subtopics.lessonTitle: Use seed-set distribution to investigate exposure without inventing parentage
subtopics.goal: Measure where seed set occurs, when it became visible and how its distribution relates to internal sources, external-risk sectors and plant developmental stage.

measure.unit: % sampled flowers/branches with developing or mature seed
measure.method: Use a defined sampling method and count sampled units with confirmed seed development separately from suspect swelling.
measure.frequency: At defined late-flower checkpoints and when unexpected seed set is found.

measure.unit: count per flower/branch or defined sample mass
measure.method: Count confirmed seeds within the same sampling unit. Keep destructive samples traceable to plant/branch ID.
measure.frequency: At investigation sampling and harvest-quality assessment.

measure.method: Map seeded units by plant and branch orientation, including edge/interior and source-facing direction when known.
Use a consistent visual/physical maturity class and preserve representative images or samples.

record: first date seed set was noticed
compare: seed-set incidence near vs far from internal source locations
source-facing vs opposite crop edges where relevant
plants with vs without observed intersex expression
seed-set pattern across timing and flowering-stage cohorts
interpret: Seed distribution can narrow hypotheses but does not identify the pollen parent by itself.
Localized seed set near a confirmed internal source differs from broad edge-biased seed set during strong external-source overlap, but either pattern can have alternative explanations.
Seed maturity can help reconstruct approximate pollination timing only within biological uncertainty; it should not be converted into an exact pollination date without validated developmental data.
subtopics.decisionRule: Classify seed-set origin as intended, probable internal, probable external or unresolved only when the evidence supports that level. Keep parentage uncertain unless direct breeding records or genetic testing establish it.
subtopics.confidenceCheck: Field pattern, wind and timing are circumstantial evidence. Genetic parentage analysis is required for high-confidence donor identification when multiple possible pollen sources exist.

fieldWorksheet.outcome: The learner should finish with a reproductive evidence chain that separates sex-expression observation, internal pollen release, external drift risk and seed-set distribution while keeping parentage uncertainty explicit.

calculationHelpers.name: Intersex-expression incidence
calculationHelpers.formula: plants with confirmed or suspect intersex structures ÷ plants inspected × 100
calculationHelpers.use: Track how widespread unexpected sex expression is within a defined scouting population.
calculationHelpers.boundary: Confirmed and suspect observations should be calculated separately when identification confidence differs.

calculationHelpers.name: Wind-source overlap
calculationHelpers.formula: source-sector upwind observations ÷ total defined wind observations × 100
calculationHelpers.use: Describe how often the external source sector was upwind during the overlap window.
calculationHelpers.boundary: This is a risk-context metric, not pollen deposition probability.

calculationHelpers.name: Phenology overlap
calculationHelpers.formula: end of shared reproductive window − start of shared reproductive window
calculationHelpers.use: Compare timing compatibility among possible pollen sources and susceptible crop flowering.
calculationHelpers.boundary: Observed or reported flowering windows may be uncertain and should be labeled accordingly.

calculationHelpers.name: Seed-set incidence
calculationHelpers.use: Track how widespread confirmed seed development is in a defined sampling frame.
calculationHelpers.boundary: Incidence does not identify the pollen source or quantify all seeds in the crop.
